chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Duwayl ibn Harun from Abu Waddad al-Hannat from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever performs the ritual bath on Friday and says: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and make me among those who repent and make me among those who purify themselves,' then purity is granted to him from one Friday until the next Friday.

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٌ عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ: Muhammad is His servant and Messenger

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing Friday bath and reciting this specific supplication?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, Friday (Yawm al-Jumu'ah) is considered the 'Eid of the Ahl al-Bayt,' making this ghusl a highly emphasized act of worship rather than merely a preparatory ritual. The supplication explicitly links the Prophet Muhammad and his purified Household (Ahl al-Bayt), reflecting the Imami emphasis on their spiritual authority in the process of purification. This practice ensures that the believer maintains a state of spiritual cleanliness and divine favor throughout the week, culminating in the next Friday's gathering.
